html:
A French post founded in 1857 on the Cap-Vert peninsula, which in 1902 became the capital of French West Africa, replacing Saint-Louis.

Its deep harbour, the westernmost in Africa, made it a naval base and a port for ships to South America. The railway linked it to the interior. It was one of the Four Communes whose people had French voting rights, and it became the political and intellectual centre of the region, home to the university named after Cheikh Anta Diop. It hosted the World Festival of Black Arts in 1966. Greater Dakar now holds about a quarter of Senegal's people.
